content.title: About
content.content: Cheese crackers are crunchy biscuits made with grated cheese incorporated into the dough. They are typically prepared from wheat or rye flour, butter, salt, and seasonings, with cheese giving them a distinctive creamy flavor and a golden hue. The snack is popular as a light bite, a complement to soups and salads, and as a beer accompaniment.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheese‑cracker recipe appeared in Europe in the 19th century.
There are more than 30 flavor variations, ranging from cheddar to parmesan and blue cheese.
Cheese crackers are often used as a base for canapés and party appetizers.
They can be baked or fried; baked versions are considered more diet‑friendly.
In some countries they are called “cheese sticks” or “cheese crisps.”

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cheese component is rich in calcium, which supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Cheese adds a modest amount of complete protein useful for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D from the cheese aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Cheese crackers typically contain no added sugars, making them suitable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 from dairy is important for nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should avoid the product.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese crackers are often salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of butter and cheese, the snack is relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional crackers contain wheat, making them unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese crackers can be enjoyed straight from the pack, served with soups, used as a base for canapés, crumbled into salads, or paired with dips. Their sturdy texture makes them convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. For longer storage (over 3 months) keep refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
